claim: A real collaborative scenario branch graph retains stable ancestry, content, revision metadata, and integrity failures through portable export, local import persistence, and disconnected reopen.
verified: The fixture uses the production scenario domain model rather than placeholder values in the scenarios collection
One root, two sibling branches, and one nested branch retain exact stable parent identities
Scenario background, workflow state, ordered turns, immutable turn revisions, edits, and attribution round-trip exactly
Portable import rebinds the Drive-origin manifest to local transport without changing shared scenario state
The imported Yjs document persists through the production LocalProjectProvider and reopens from IndexedDB without a network provider
The complete graph inspector projection is identical before export, after decode, and after disconnected reopen
Deleting the root before export produces missing-parent failures that remain identical after import instead of being laundered
Existing archive corruption, identity, collision, size, and orphan-state gates remain green
limitations: The proof uses fake IndexedDB in one headless process; it does not reproduce a packaged transfer between two physical installations.
The archive is an offline handoff and does not preserve a live Drive collaboration connection after import.
This proves exact graph transport and integrity retention, not a dedicated scenario-pack schema or selective scenario export.
Malformed graph state remains visible and read-only after import; the archive decoder does not silently repair research history.
